text:
The Penguins are winless in four, outscored 14-6, and the conversation around them has moved from the standings to the exits. General manager Kyle Dubas has been open to moving veterans, TSN's Pierre LeBrun reported that Rickard Rakell's no-trade list stopped a deal with Chicago, and the headlines have run through Erik Karlsson, Rakell and even Sidney Crosby, who keeps being linked to Montreal. Crosby is still here, still Pittsburgh's center, and our numbers have him at 32% to score tonight.

The good news for him is Evgeni Malkin, off the out list and day to day. When Bryan Rust went down (he's out until December), it was Malkin who moved up beside Crosby and Rakell, at nearly 20 minutes a night. Malkin, 40, is having a fine year (our numbers make him 71% for a point), and that makes him a trade name too. The bad news is the net. Arturs Silovs is 0-5-0 over his last five starts with a .857 save rate and 3.8 goals worse than expected. Pittsburgh still controls play more often than not (52% of five-on-five expected goals, the quality of chances each side gets), which is why their 16 points look worse than the 23.5 our numbers say they've earned.

Calgary has fewer excuses on the process side. The Flames take 46% of the expected goals and are winless in three (0-2-1). Dustin Wolf, the goalie they built around, is at .877 and 6.5 goals worse than expected. Martin Pospisil is out after the hit that got Wyatt Kaiser suspended three games, and Kevin Bahl is out too. Connor Zary is off the injury report, which helps. Matt Coronato is our sleeper for a point at 59%, because his ice time is up to a projected 19:15, and fourth-liner Aydar Suniev has been getting to dangerous spots.

Both teams sit at 7% to make the playoffs. This is the kind of game where what happens matters less than who's still on the roster at the deadline on March 1.
headline: In Pittsburgh, the trade talk is louder than the games
